title: Troubleshooting Clusters, Nodes and Components

header.html: Troubleshoot clusters and nodes; Troubleshoot cluster components
Kubernetes v1.37.0 (kubeadm-style kind nodes; breakage and repair done through docker exec, which stands in for ssh <node> on the exam)

toc.title: The node: kubelet and container runtime
The control plane: static Pods and crictl
A checklist for any "cluster is broken" task

html:
1First look at the cluster

k get nodes -o wide                    # STATUS: Ready / NotReady / SchedulingDisabled
k describe node <n>                    # Conditions (Ready, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure) and Events
k get pods -n kube-system -o wide      # control plane and add-on Pods
k get --raw /readyz?verbose            # API server health checks, one per line
k cluster-info

Decide which layer is broken before you touch anything:

Symptom Layer Where to look
kubectl says "connection refused" or hangs API server, or your kubeconfig kubeconfig server address; API server container on the control plane node
kubectl works, one node NotReady that node's kubelet or runtime ssh <node>; systemctl status kubelet containerd; journalctl -u kubelet
kubectl works, new Pods stay Pending with no node scheduler (or cordoned/tainted nodes) kube-scheduler container; k get nodes
Deployment exists but no ReplicaSet/Pods controller manager kube-controller-manager container
Pods run but a Service/DNS fails networking Module 13

2The node: kubelet and container runtime

Two systemd services keep a node Ready: kubelet and containerd. NotReady means the kubelet stopped reporting or cannot work.

ssh <node>
sudo -i
systemctl status kubelet               # active? enabled? last log lines
systemctl is-active kubelet containerd
journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail -30     # why it failed (-f to follow)
systemctl enable --now kubelet         # start now AND at boot
systemctl restart kubelet              # after you change its config
Cause Evidence Fix
kubelet stopped or disabled (Lab 12.1) inactive (dead) systemctl enable --now kubelet
bad kubelet configuration (Lab 12.2) journal: "failed to load kubelet config" / strict decoding error naming the field fix /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml, systemctl restart kubelet
runtime stopped (Lab 12.7) kubelet is active, journal: runtime/CRI errors; node NotReady systemctl enable --now containerd
wrong certificate or kubeconfig path journal: x509 / "no such file" fix the path in /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf or the cert file
wrong API server address journal: connection refused to the address fix server: in /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf
CNI missing node NotReady, "network plugin not ready" install or fix the CNI (/etc/cni/net.d)
disk, memory or PID pressure describe node Conditions free space, evict, resize

The kubelet config file is /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml (static Pod path, cgroup driver, DNS); its service flags come from a systemd drop-in (systemctl cat kubelet shows all files); its connection to the API server is /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf. systemctl cat kubelet is the fastest way to find which files are involved.

A NotReady node's Pods stay Running in the API for a while (a grace period) and are then evicted; do not wait: fix the node.

3The control plane: static Pods and crictl

In a kubeadm cluster the API server, scheduler, controller manager and etcd are static Pods. Their manifests are in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/. The kubelet restarts a component when its manifest changes, so fixing a component means editing its manifest on the control plane node.

When the API server is down, kubectl is useless, so use the node tools:

ssh <control-plane>
crictl ps -a --name kube-apiserver                 # state: Running / Exited (and how many attempts)
crictl logs $(crictl ps -a --name kube-apiserver -q | head -1) 2>&1 | tail   # the last error
ls /etc/kubernetes/manifests /etc/kubernetes/pki
grep -n "etcd-servers\|tls-cert-file" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail           # the kubelet reports static Pod problems too

Find the typo, correct it in the manifest (the kubelet restarts the component), and wait: the API server needs about 30 to 60 seconds. Do not copy the file out and back; edit in place. Keep a backup before editing: cp kube-apiserver.yaml /tmp/.

Broken component Symptom Usual breakage in the manifest
kube-apiserver (Labs 12.3, 12.4) kubectl refused or timeouts; container Exited or unready wrong --etcd-servers port, wrong cert/key file name, wrong flag spelling, bad --service-cluster-ip-range
kube-scheduler (Lab 12.5) new Pods Pending, no node chosen, no events from the scheduler wrong --kubeconfig path, bad flag
kube-controller-manager (Lab 12.6) Deployments get no ReplicaSet/Pods; nodes do not recover; PVCs unbound wrong --root-ca-file, cert path, flag
etcd API server cannot start, "etcdserver" errors wrong data dir, wrong cert path, peer/client URLs

Do not "work around" (set nodeName by hand, create Pods directly): the task asks for the component to be repaired, and the check looks at the component.

4Your own access: kubeconfig problems

If only you cannot reach the cluster, check your kubeconfig before the cluster (Lab 12.8):

k config view --minify                 # server address, user, namespace of the current context
k config get-contexts
k config set-cluster <name> --server=https://<right-address>:6443
k config use-context <name>
k --kubeconfig /path/to/file get nodes

The admin kubeconfig on a control plane node is /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf. "connection refused" = nothing listens at that address and port (wrong server or API server down); "Unauthorized" or "forbidden" = credentials or RBAC; "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" = wrong CA data.

5Not broken, just switched off

  • SchedulingDisabled in k get nodes means the node is cordoned. Pods may stay Pending when all nodes are cordoned or tainted (Lab 12.9). Fix: k uncordon <node>.
  • A taint you did not expect (k describe node | grep Taints) keeps Pods away; see Module 6.
  • Resource pressure shows in the node Conditions.

6Certificates (quick check)

kubeadm certs check-expiration lists expiry dates. An expired certificate gives x509 errors in component logs and in kubectl. Renewal is kubeadm certs renew all followed by restarting the control plane Pods (Module 3).

7A checklist for any "cluster is broken" task

  1. Is the problem in kubectl (kubeconfig) or the cluster? k --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf get nodes on the control plane node.
  2. k get nodes, then k get pods -A | grep -v Running.
  3. For a node: ssh, systemctl status, journalctl -u kubelet.
  4. For a component: crictl ps -a, crictl logs, the manifest.
  5. Fix the root cause, wait, and verify with the original symptom (k get nodes, create a test Pod).

8Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m12 -->

Lab 12.1: kubelet stopped

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-01-kubelet-stopped)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Node cka-worker shows NotReady. Find the cause and fix it so the node is Ready. The fix must survive a restart of the node (the kubelet service must be enabled and running). Hint: ssh cka-worker, then sudo -i; look at systemctl and journalctl.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-worker 'systemctl status kubelet --no-pager | head -5'
ssh cka-worker 'systemctl enable --now kubelet'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/cka-worker --timeout=120s

Lab 12.2: kubelet config

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-02-kubelet-config)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The node cka-worker went NotReady after someone edited the kubelet configuration. Find the problem in the kubelet logs, fix the configuration file /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml on that node, and bring the node back to Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-worker 'systemctl status kubelet --no-pager | head -8'
ssh cka-worker 'journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | grep -i -E "yaml|failed|error" | tail -3'
ssh cka-worker 'sed -i "/^broken:/d" /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml && systemctl restart kubelet'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/cka-worker --timeout=180s

Lab 12.3: apiserver etcd flag

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 9 | Time: about 10 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-03-apiserver-etcd-flag)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

kubectl commands fail or time out: the API server is not healthy. Connect to the control plane node cka-control-plane, find the cause (container logs with crictl, the static Pod manifest) and fix it. When done, kubectl get nodes must work again.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl ps -a --name kube-apiserver'
ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl logs $(crictl ps -a --name kube-apiserver -q | head -1) 2>&1 | tail -5'
ssh cka-control-plane 'grep etcd-servers /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'sed -i "s#--etcd-servers=https://127.0.0.1:2381#--etcd-servers=https://127.0.0.1:2379#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'systemctl restart kubelet'   # resets the crash-loop back-off of the static Pod
until kubectl get --raw /readyz >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done

Lab 12.4: apiserver cert path

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 9 | Time: about 10 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-04-apiserver-cert-path)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

kubectl reports "connection refused": the API server container does not even start. On the control plane node cka-control-plane, find out why (look at the container list with crictl ps -a and its logs) and repair the problem. When done, kubectl get nodes must work.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl ps -a --name kube-apiserver'
ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl logs $(crictl ps -a --name kube-apiserver -q | head -1) 2>&1 | tail -4'
ssh cka-control-plane 'sed -i "s#apiserver.crt.bak#apiserver.crt#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'systemctl restart kubelet'   # resets the crash-loop back-off of the static Pod
until kubectl get --raw /readyz >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done

Lab 12.5: scheduler broken

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-05-scheduler-broken)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

New Pods in the namespace sched1 stay Pending with no node assigned (the Deployment probe-app has 2 replicas). Existing workloads are fine. Find the faulty control plane component on cka-control-plane and repair it so that both Pods are scheduled and become Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl ps -a --name kube-scheduler'
ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl logs $(crictl ps -a --name kube-scheduler -q | head -1) 2>&1 | tail -3'
ssh cka-control-plane 'sed -i "s#scheduler.cnf#scheduler.conf#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'systemctl restart kubelet'   # resets the crash-loop back-off of the static Pod
kubectl -n sched1 rollout status deployment probe-app --timeout=180s

Lab 12.6: controller manager broken

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-06-controller-manager-broken)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace cm1, the Deployment counter (2 replicas) was created but no Pods appear and kubectl get rs shows nothing. Find the faulty control plane component on cka-control-plane and repair it so that both Pods run.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl ps -a --name kube-controller-manager'
ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl logs $(crictl ps -a --name kube-controller-manager -q | head -1) 2>&1 | tail -3'
ssh cka-control-plane 'sed -i "s#ca.crtx#ca.crt#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'systemctl restart kubelet'   # resets the crash-loop back-off of the static Pod
kubectl -n cm1 rollout status deployment counter --timeout=180s

Lab 12.7: containerd stopped

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-07-containerd-stopped)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The node cka-worker2 is NotReady; the kubelet is running but cannot talk to the container runtime. Fix the node so it is Ready again, and make sure the runtime service is enabled and running.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-worker2 'systemctl is-active kubelet; systemctl is-active containerd'
ssh cka-worker2 'journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail -3'
ssh cka-worker2 'systemctl enable --now containerd'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/cka-worker2 --timeout=180s

Lab 12.8: kubeconfig wrong server

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-08-kubeconfig-wrong-server)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The file ~/answers/broken.kubeconfig is a copy of a working kubeconfig, but kubectl --kubeconfig ~/answers/broken.kubeconfig get nodes fails with a connection error. Fix the file (use kubectl config commands; keep the cluster, user and context names) so that the command works again.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl --kubeconfig ~/answers/broken.kubeconfig get nodes 2>&1 | tail -2
good=$(kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}')
kubectl config set-cluster kind-cka --server=$good --kubeconfig ~/answers/broken.kubeconfig
kubectl --kubeconfig ~/answers/broken.kubeconfig get nodes

Lab 12.9: cordoned nodes

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m12-09-cordoned-nodes)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace cord, the Deployment queue (2 replicas) has Pods that stay Pending. The Pods have no resource problems. Find the cause and fix the cluster so that both Pods run (do not change the Deployment).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get nodes
kubectl -n cord describe pod -l app=queue | grep -i -A2 FailedScheduling | head -4
kubectl uncordon cka-worker cka-worker2
kubectl -n cord rollout status deployment queue --timeout=120s

<!-- /LABS -->

9Recall questions

R1A node is NotReady. Which two services do you check first?

Show the answer

kubelet and containerd (systemctl status, journalctl -u kubelet).

R2kubectl is refused. Which tool inspects the API server container?

Show the answer

crictl ps -a and crictl logs on the control plane node.

R3Where do you fix a broken control plane component?

Show the answer

In its static Pod manifest in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/; the kubelet restarts it.

R4New Pods stay Pending with no node assigned and existing Pods are fine. Which component?

Show the answer

The scheduler.

R5A Deployment shows no ReplicaSet. Which component?

Show the answer

The controller manager.

R6What does SchedulingDisabled mean and how do you undo it?

Show the answer

The node is cordoned; kubectl uncordon <node>.

R7What does "connection refused" tell you about the API server address?

Show the answer

Nothing is listening there: wrong server in the kubeconfig or the API server is down.

R8What is the difference between systemctl start kubelet and systemctl enable --now kubelet?

Show the answer

start runs it now; enable --now also starts it at every boot.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Node NotReady kubelet, containerd, journalctl -u kubelet, CNI
Kubelet files /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml, /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf, systemctl cat kubelet
Control plane fix edit the manifest in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/; kubelet restarts it
API server down crictl ps -a, crictl logs, check etcd flags and cert paths
Symptoms Pending no node = scheduler; no ReplicaSet = controller manager; refused = API server or kubeconfig
Cordoned SchedulingDisabled -> uncordon
Always back up the manifest, fix the root cause, verify the original symptom
